transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I came in because my husband made me. Him and the people down at the warehouse keep acting like I'm... like I'm crazy or something. But I'm not. I know for a fact they've been watching my every move on the floor and changing my pallet counts just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

Which is just wrong, you know? Because I work harder than any of them. Like, just the other day I was loading this huge order of dog food, and they got this new forklift in—well, it's not new, it's used, but it's new to us—and the seat on it is just completely busted. I told Jerry, he's the guy who's supposed to fix the machines, though honestly he mostly just sits out in his truck smoking those cheap cigars... I told him he needs to fix the spring in that seat because my lower back is just killing me. I actually had to go to Walmart on my break to buy one of those gel cushions just to make it through the shift. They had them on clearance, which was nice, but still. 

But yeah... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. My husband. He thinks I'm making it up about them changing my numbers at work, so he told me I had to come talk to you.
How much sleep have you been getting each night lately?

Sleep? I mean, I don't really need much. There have been weeks lately where I sleep maybe... three hours a night? And I'll just wake up way before my alarm even goes off, but I feel completely fine. Like I don't need any more rest at all to get moving and start my day. 

Which is a good thing, honestly, because my alarm is just my cell phone, and I actually had to get the screen fixed last weekend. My cat, Buster—he's this huge orange tabby I found out by the loading docks last winter—he knocked it right off the nightstand. I had to take it to that little kiosk in the mall, you know, the one right across from the Auntie Anne's pretzels? The guy there wanted eighty bucks just to replace the glass. Eighty bucks! I told him he was out of his mind, I could buy a whole new phone at MetroPCS for that kind of money. The pretzels smelled really good though. I almost bought one of the cinnamon sugar ones, but the line was just way too long and I had to get back to run some errands. 

But yeah, I don't know why my husband makes such a big deal out of how much I sleep. Three hours is plenty, I pop right out of bed and I'm good to go.
Before this started, have you ever had a time in your life when you felt very down, sad, or lost interest in things for several weeks?

Down or sad? No, I don't think so. I haven't really had anything like that where I just sit around. I don't have time for that anyway, I like to stay busy, you know? 

I mean, I guess I lose interest in some things, but just normal things. Like, I used to be really into baking, but then the heating element in our oven burned out. It literally just sparked and went totally black right in the middle of making a batch of peanut butter cookies. My landlord said he'd send a guy out to look at it, but he always uses this same handyman, Rick, who takes absolutely forever to show up. Rick drives this beat-up old Chevy Silverado, the paint is just peeling right off the hood, and he parked it halfway across my driveway last time he was here to fix the leaky faucet in the bathroom. My husband couldn't even get his car out to go to work. He was so mad, he had to go knock on the neighbor's door to see if they knew where Rick went, because Rick had just wandered off to take a phone call or something. 

But anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being sad. No, I don't really get down like that. I feel fine.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

Well, yeah, sometimes... I mean, I hear things. Like when I'm walking down the aisle at the warehouse, or even just at home folding laundry, I'll hear this man's voice. Clear as day, he just says, "Nicole, check it again." And I look around, and there's nobody there. 

Which is weird, right? Because I do the laundry on Tuesdays, usually right after I get off my shift, and I always use that Tide with the Downy built-in. The liquid kind, not the pods. I tried the pods once because they were on sale at Dollar General, but they didn't dissolve right in my washer. My washer is one of those top-loaders, older model, and it gets off balance if you put too many towels in it. It'll just start banging around like crazy, making this awful racket, and you have to run over and push the lid down to stop it so you can rearrange everything. My husband tried to level it out by putting a piece of cardboard under the front leg, but it still does it if I wash the heavy bathroom rugs. I bought those rugs at Target, they're this really pretty teal color, but they hold so much water... 

But yeah, the voice. It just tells me to check things again, even when I'm all alone.
Before this started, have you ever had another time in your life where you felt this full of energy and needed very little sleep?

Yeah, I mean... these stretches where I feel totally wired, where I barely sleep and just take on way too much stuff? They've been coming and going for about six months now. 

It's actually kind of helpful at work, honestly. Being a material mover at the warehouse, you're on your feet all day, lifting boxes, scanning pallets, moving things from the receiving dock to the storage racks. We use these hand trucks, the heavy-duty metal ones with the big rubber wheels, but the bearings on mine have been squeaking like crazy lately. I asked the floor manager, Dave, if I could get a can of WD-40 from the maintenance closet, but he said he lost the key. Dave is always losing his keys. He lost his car keys last month and had to wait in the breakroom for three hours for his wife to bring him the spare. She brought their kids with her, and the youngest one, he must have been like four or five, he managed to get his hand stuck in the vending machine trying to pull out a bag of Cool Ranch Doritos. It was a whole big thing, they almost had to call the fire department, but Dave finally wiggled the kid's arm loose. 

But yeah, the energy thing. It's been happening on and off for about six months. I just get so much done, you know?
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or over-the-counter medications recently?

No, I don't really drink or do drugs or anything. I mean, I'll take a Tylenol if my back is acting up from work, but that's about it. 

I actually had to buy a new bottle of Tylenol just last week because my husband left the old one in the glove compartment of his car, and it got all melted and weird. He drives this 2012 Ford Focus, and the AC has been broken for like two years. We took it to this mechanic down on 4th Street, right next to that old bowling alley that shut down? The bowling alley got bought out by some developer who wants to turn it into luxury apartments, which is ridiculous because who's going to pay luxury prices to live next to a tire shop and a Dollar Tree? But anyway, the mechanic said it was the compressor, and he wanted like eight hundred bucks to fix it. My husband was like, "No way, I'll just roll the windows down." But then when it rains, you can't roll the windows down, and the windshield fogs up so bad you can't even see the road. He tried using that Rain-X stuff on the inside of the glass, but it just made it all streaky and weird when the headlights hit it at night. 

So yeah, no drugs or alcohol or anything like that. Just regular stuff when I need it.
Have you ever heard that voice during times when your energy was completely normal?

Yeah, I do. Even when things are quiet... like a few weeks ago, I was actually sleeping pretty normal, not racing around or anything, and I still heard that man's voice. He was still telling me to check things. And I just knew, I knew somebody was messing with the pallet counts at work, trying to set me up or something. 

Which is a huge deal, because if your counts are off, they write you up. And they use these new scanners, the Motorola ones with the touchscreen? They're supposed to be better, but half the time the battery dies right in the middle of a shift. You have to go all the way back to the charging station in the breakroom, and the cords are always tangled up. Someone brought in zip ties to try and keep them organized, but Dave—the manager I told you about—he accidentally cut one of the actual charging cables when he was trying to snip a zip tie. He had to tape it back together with electrical tape, the black kind, but it doesn't really work right anymore. If you bump the scanner while it's in that cradle, it just stops charging. And then you're stuck out on the floor in aisle 12, trying to scan a skid of dog food, and the screen just goes black. I hate that dog food, by the way. It's the big 50-pound bags, and they always stack them too high so the bottom bags get crushed and leak kibble everywhere. Then the warehouse mice get into it... 

But yeah, even when my energy was totally fine and I was sleeping, the voice was still there, and I still knew about the pallets.

I remember because I had to buy a new winter coat. I went to that Burlington Coat Factory out by the highway, the one next to the Olive Garden. It had this faux fur around the hood, which I thought looked really nice, but every time it rained or snowed, the fur would get all matted and look like a wet dog. And the zipper was one of those cheap plastic ones, you know? It kept catching on the fabric on the inside. I tried rubbing a bar of soap on the teeth of the zipper because my grandmother told me that helps lubricate it, but it just made my coat smell like Irish Spring. My grandmother used to use Irish Spring for everything, she even put bars of it in her garden to keep the deer away from her tomato plants. She grew these massive beefsteak tomatoes, they were so big you could make a whole sandwich out of just one slice... 

But yeah, it's been about eight months since all the voices and the watching started.
